reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on jigs and minnows in 18-28 feet over brush.
reports.by: Randy Britton, The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on live minnows close to structure.
reports.by: Hundley's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Dock knockers and small clousers should be producing bass and crappie around retaining walls.
reports.by: Guide Alex Guthrie, Fly Fish Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Morning bass bite is good around pond weed with frogs and flukes and shaky heads at the edge in 2-4 feet.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Mitchell's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Catfish, stripers, and black bass are also slow, and with water temperatures holding around 91 degrees, even bank fishing has been tough.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie bite is good on the bridge, dock poles and brush piles. Largemouth bite is decent early morning on topwaters then switching over to jigs, deep crankbaits and Texas rigged baits near docks and main lake points. White bass and hybrids are good on main lake humps with slabs or trolling. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good to 3.63 pounds in 18-25 feet of water on shaky heads with green pumpkin F5 worms, dropshots with 6-inch worms in Morning Glory, whopper ploppers and square bill crankbaits. Crappie are good to 13 inches on minnows and jigs in 10-20 feet on deeper large docks with brush on the main lake and on scattered brush piles. White bass are fair to 1.25 pounds on crappie jigs and minnows out of the lights at night.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing remains steady as fish continue setting up in their late-summer patterns.
reports.by: Landon Hernandez, Aggie Anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Bass are schooling up and can be caught with flukes, Pop-Rs, buzzbaits and frogs on main lake and up in river/bayou spots. Pads and grass are getting thick as the water level drops so in all your spots look for the birds or bait and you should find bass to fish for.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Water normal stain; 94 degrees; Redfish action has been excellent throughout the lake in 5-25 feet of water, with anglers finding success both trolling and casting using gold and silver Johnson Sprite spoons, Academy spoons, H&H, Hoagie Baits, DOA and Bass Assassins in a variety of colors. Striper and black bass remain slow, though bank fishermen are reporting a few redfish in the 5-10 pound range on live tilapia around Spider Island and Picnic Point.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Bank anglers are finding good action on blue and channel catfish, with white bass also biting well and crappie showing up at times. Black bass has been fair, but overall fishing is steady for those working from the bank.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Coleman fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 2.75 pounds are fair in 10-20 feet of water around the lake off points with a scope minnow and in the shade of the docks on shaky heads with F5 worms in red bug and green pumpkin. Crappie are excellent to 14 inches on minnows in 8-15 feet under docks in Rattlesnake Cove on the right side going in.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing remains slow, with most catches coming on soft plastics worked in 6-12 feet of water.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been a little tough like everything else, but deeper docks and offshore structures can produce some nice ones. Crappie are finicky, but folks are picking up decent ones, finding them on structure and standing timber in 14-20 feet. Hybrids and whites are schooling well and providing good action, being productive using slabs, spoons or shad, finding them on flats and the edge of drop-offs in 15-22 feet.
reports.by: Bradley Doyle, Bradley's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Morning bass bite is shallow for a couple of hours around grass and bream beds. Mid morning target bass offshore a bit in 5-7 feet, 2.5 square bills are good around flats with lots of baitfish around. Bass are beginning to school, a hard-bodied popper should work well.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Mitchell's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good to 7 pounds working creek entrances and shaded docks using soft plastics and crankbaits. Crappie action has been good to excellent on small minnows fished near underwater structures. Look for crappie suspended on structure in 15 feet of water.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth are snapping on the docks and riprap along with drains and points eating crankbaits and spinnerbaits. Crappie are fantastic on brush piles from 6-10 feet eating hand tied jigs and minnows.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite is still tough, but some are being caught on topwater shallow, and on soft plastics on deeper brush piles and structure.
reports.by: Greg Lotun

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 15-20 feet of water with minnows and chartreuse jigs.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good early and late off points with hydrilla. Crappie are good suspended on brush and timber in 20-25 feet.
reports.by: Hambone Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is great with sand bass caught everywhere around the lake morning, day and night. Blue crankbaits, shad fat free fingerling and minnows have been effective for both largemouth and smallmouth. Crappie fishing is fair with catches in the Sanford Yake area off the dock.
reports.by: Dave Wright, Wright-On Bait, Tackle and Watercraft Rental

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Bass are excellent on Carolina rig worms and ribbon tail Texas worms around 14-20 feet of water. Bass are offshore near the creek channels in 30-40 fish schools. Crappie are good with bigger fish in timber, and smaller fish in the brush with smaller crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie numbers remain solid, while catfish have been slow.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are biting in deep water on minnows. Black bass, hybrids and sand bass are slow.
reports.by: David Holt, Lake Palo Pinto RV Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent, slowly fishing a solid white crappie jig. Crappie ranging from 1.5-2 pounds can be found in 15-20 fish groups in standing timber. Bass are good on dropshots and large swimbaits on main points or suspended in the middle of the lake.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are still holding in their summer patterns on main lake docks and brush piles.
reports.by: Terry Hawkins Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are being caught shallow on points and pockets with topwater frogs and Senkos, while crankbaits are working on points and drains, and jigs or Carolina rigs are producing off ledges and structure. Crappie are starting to stack up on brush and timber, white bass are schooling off points, and catfish have moved into deeper water and creek channels where cut bait is working well.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At the marina, crappie bite is fair, bluegill are fair on crickets and worms, and catfish are good on minnows and punch bait. On the lake, crappie are fair on jigs and minnows over brush in 8-15 feet of water with late afternoon bite good. Black bass are fair on crankbaits and soft plastic baits in 6-14 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Keep a Cork Rig with Sandy Sandwich streamer handy for eruptions of topwater feeding by schoolie-sized largemouth and white bass. Fish have been shallow since it flooded but with the water receding, the bass have moved back out.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Mostly catching them on slabs. Slabs, topwaters and swimbaits are producing fish when you get on the right school. Crappie fishing - look at brush near the mouths of coves and creeks in 15-20 feet of water.
reports.by: John Blasingame, Adventure Texoma Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are up in the main lake in brush in 15-20 feet of water. White bass fishing is poor on slabs on main lake humps in 15-25 feet of water. Largemouth bass fishing is good using soft plastics on deep structure.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Report by Kurt Dove, Amistad Bass Guide
reports.by: Kurt Dove, Amistad Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite has been solid early in the morning on topwaters and crankbaits. As the day progresses, bass are transitioning to points and brush piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: There continues to be a decent grass bite for bass with lightweight Texas rig worms fished slowly along the edges.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been feeding on points and doing a lot of surface feeding. A few bigger bass have been caught on structure in 15-20 feet of water. Crappie have been slow to bite but minnows and jigs are both doing OK. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide. Dock knockers and small clousers should be producing bass and crappie around retaining walls.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Early morning bass bite has slowed down but pondweed is the ticket for a shallow bite.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Mitchell's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Catfish and stripers have been slow, while black bass fishing off the bank has been excellent at times, with live tilapia producing the best results.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie bite is good on the bridge, dock poles and brush piles. Largemouth bite is decent using jigs, deep crankbaits and wacky rigged baits near deep docks and main lake points. White bass and hybrids are good on main lake humps with slabs or trolling. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good to 5.63 pounds in 18-25 feet of water on shaky heads with green pumpkin F5 worms, dropshots with 6-inch worms in Morning Glory, whopper ploppers and square bill crankbaits. Crappie are good to 11 inches on minnows and jigs in 12-25 feet on deeper large docks with brush on the main lake and on scattered brush piles. White bass are fair to 1.25 pounds on crappie jigs and minnows out of the lights at night.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Stripers have been slow, while black bass fishing off the bank has been excellent at times with live baits, tilapia, crawfish, and shrimp producing the best results.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Bank fishing in certain areas is excellent, with catfish in the channels, blues, crappie, and stripers all being caught.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has been slow, with most action occurring in the early morning using soft plastics around wood.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are active around deeper docks, offshore structures and brim beds. Schooling bass can also be found in 16-22 feet of water chasing baitfish. Crappie are finicky, finding them on structure and standing timber in 16-21 feet. Hybrids and whites are schooling well and providing good action, being productive using slabs, spoons or shad, finding them on flats and the edge of drop-offs in 12-30 feet.
reports.by: Bradley Doyle, Bradley's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been feeding on points and doing a lot of surface feeding. A few bigger bass have been caught on structure in 15-20 feet of water. Crappie have been slow to bite but minnows and jigs are both doing fair. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught mid morning in 5-7 feet on the first drop-off, tree line or point. Brush piles are the key to big bass. Lake Fork crappie fishing has been tough this summer. We are seeing huge schools of black crappie loaded up on brush piles, laydowns, tire reefs and underwater bridges. You may also need to weed through numbers of short fish to get some keeper crappie. The white crappie are on timber and some brush in 12-40 feet but you have to cover water and find the right areas holding fish.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Mitchell's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in brush piles in 12-14 feet of water on minnows and jigs. Sand bass and hybrids are schooling around the hot water outlet good on slabs and jigs. Largemouth bass are slow biting in shallow water vegetation on moving baits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing has been good to excellent on small minnows and jigs on submerged timber and bridge pilings. Largemouth bass to 6 pounds are good on rattle traps and soft plastics near shaded docks and near major creek entrances.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good to 5 pounds on worms and crankbaits fished around cover. Crappie are good on jigs and minnows fished over brush piles in 6-10 feet of water. White bass are very good to 2 pounds on slab spoons fished over main lake humps and ridges.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell's Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are in the shade late morning under docks on the main lake and up the west fork eating grubs and spinnerbaits. Crappie are biting pretty good tight to structure, eating hand tied jigs and minnows in the east fork and Luces Bayou with a few spots on the south end at the old pump house deep.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass bite has been extremely tough, finesse baits such as dropshot and shaky head are getting some bites on deeper brush piles and structure, as well as on big worms on Texas rig.
reports.by: Greg Lotun

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 12-15 feet on brush and timber using 1/16-ounce jigs in any color. Black bass are good with white and chartreuse spinnerbaits in the mornings along with jerkbaits and soft plastics like the original Slugo worked Texas rigged without weight. White slabs 1 ounce with treble hooks cut off except one work best at Little Ridge Point, Hybrid Point and the island tip. Tying a jig 12 inches above your slab on a loop knot catches two fish at a time.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Marble Falls fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with medium diving crankbaits or paddle tail swimbaits fished around rock.
reports.by: Tyler Torwick, Torwick's Guiding Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good early and late on Texas rigged worms off points and along the hydrilla. Crappie are good suspended in brush piles and standing timber in 20-25 feet. For large catfish, use large live bait under the schools of crappie.
reports.by: Hambone Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on Texas rigs and Carolina rigs on creek channel swings in groups of 15-20 at a time. Crappie are also good - the bigger ones are on the timber, smaller ones in those secondary brush piles on chartreuse and white crappie jigs. Bass are excellent on Carolina rigs on secondary main lake points. Crappie are excellent with a lot of them in groups on timber with white and chartreuse crappie jigs. Big ones with a lot of fish over one and a half pounds - they are big crappie right now and we've been having awesome crappie fishing trips.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie populations remain strong, while catfish have been slow.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair to 7 pounds on topwater frogs and whopper ploppers. Crappie are picking up good around timber 12-14 feet deep suspended.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Black bass and crappie are slow with few anglers reporting catches.
reports.by: David Holt, Lake Palo Pinto RV Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on dropshots and large swimbaits on main points or suspended in the middle of the lake. Crappie are fair on white and chartreuse jigs or live minnows.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: The action doesn't last long, but they will hit spinners and slabs. The black bass are on main lake docks and brush piles.
reports.by: Terry Hawkins Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At the marina, crappie bite is fair, bluegill are fair on crickets and worms, and catfish are fair on minnows and punch bait. On the lake, crappie are fair on jigs and minnows over brush in 8-15 feet of water with late afternoon bite good. Black bass are fair on crankbaits and soft plastic baits in 6-14 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Topwaters, swimbaits and slabs are producing. In the hot days of summer utilize electronics to locate active crappie near brush and structure in 18-25 feet of water near coves and creeks.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Crappie remain slow, but with cooler temperatures expected this weekend and into next week, both bass and crappie action should improve.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: The most consistent bass fishing is deep.
reports.by: Tyler Torwick, Torwick's Guiding Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows in 16 feet of water. Bass are fair on crankbaits.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on structure in 10-18 feet of water. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.
reports.by: Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good over brush in 18-28 feet using jigs and minnows.
reports.by: Randy Britton, The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on live minnows and small jigs with lots of undersized fish. Largemouth bass are fair on structure.
reports.by: Hundley's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are early morning and late evening, finding more roaming points that have early evening shade. Crappie are loaded on most structures between 10-30 feet of water, but the best bite has been on brush piles and shallow timber. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide. Dock knockers and small clousers should be producing bass and crappie around retaining walls.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass early morning bite is short but weedless poppers or frogs on pond weed is best, work flukes on the edge.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Mitchell's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Water normal stain; 94 degrees; Redfish action is good in parts of the lake, especially near the dam and in front of the power plant, with anglers having success trolling and casting golden or silver spoons as well as a wide variety of plastics, including H&H and Bass Assassin, in 10-15 feet of water. Stripers, black bass, and catfish remain slow, but bank fishing for redfish with live bait has been excellent at times.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good to 5.65 pounds in 4-25 feet of water on dropshots with a 6-inch worm in Morning Glory, 7-inch worms and square bill cranks and topwater around the grass. Crappie are good to 12 inches on minnows and jigs in 8-25 feet on deeper large docks with brush on the main lake and on scattered brush piles. White bass are fair to 1.25 pounds on crappie jigs and minnows out of the lights at night.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Look for the birds or listen for pads that pop to help find productive spots that would be holding bass because of the bait.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Water normal stain; 95 degrees; The lake is about 2 feet low, but redfish action is excellent across all parts, especially in shallow waters 5-10 feet deep, with anglers finding success using plastics (H&H, Hoagie Bait, Bass Assassin in various colors), gold and silver spoons, both trolling and coasting. Stripers and black bass are slow at the moment, but bank fishing overall has been outstanding.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Bank fishing of the lake is producing crappie, white bass, catfish, and freshwater drum.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Fishing has been good, with catfish, bass, and especially crappie biting well at night.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: The lake is near normal pool level, and bass fishing is slow overall, though some early action can be found off extended points and around standing timber in 7-10 feet of water, with plastics continuing to produce the best results.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Bass are early morning and late evening, finding more roaming points that have early evening shade. Crappie are loaded on most structures between 10-30 feet of water, but the best bite has been on brush piles and shallow timber. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Dog days of summer are here, fish boat docks and lily pads at mid day when bass are seeking cover. Brush piles are the key to big bass.
reports.by: Guide Alex Guthrie, Fly Fish Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass and small striped bass continue to be good on most days early and late on live bait and slabs. Largemouth bass are good on topwater early and better near deeper docks and shaded areas later in the day. Crappie action is good on deeper structure and near deeper docks on the main lake using small minnows and jigs.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good on worms and crankbaits fished around cover. Crappie are good on micro jigs fished over cover in 4-12 feet of water. White bass are fair on slab spoons fished over main lake humps and ridges.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell's Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hawkins fishing report
reports.text: Topwater early and late will produce good black bass action.
reports.by: Guide Alex Guthrie, Fly Fish Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are biting well on spinnerbaits fished along the thermocline near structure. Crappie are great on the east fork and in Luces Bayou, taking hand-tied jigs and minnows tight to laydowns and stumps.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: For bass the bite is extremely tough, with numbers being caught down quite a bit.
reports.by: Greg Lotun

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair to good early and late along the hydrilla with swimbaits and Texas rigged worms. Crappie remain good in 20-25 feet suspended in brush piles using minnows.
reports.by: Hambone Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie numbers are good, while catfish remain slow.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are hit or miss. A few crappie are still coming off the docks daily.
reports.by: Navarro Mills Marina

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Black bass and crappie are slow with few reported catches.
reports.by: David Holt, Lake Palo Pinto RV Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are starting to move out deeper to deep brush in 35-40 feet and in trees in 25-40 feet of water. Largemouth bass are on offshore rocks or shallow brush. Dan's Crappie Co.
reports.by: Daniel Koberna, Lt. Dan's Crappie Co

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are in their summer patterns.
reports.by: Terry Hawkins Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At the Marina crappie bite is fair, bluegill are fair on crickets and worms, and catfish are fair on minnows and punch bait. On the lake crappie are good on jigs and minnows over brush in 8-15 feet of water with late afternoon bite good. Black bass are fair on crankbaits and soft plastic baits in 6-14 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are scattered but some nice ones are being caught deep and shallow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texana fishing report
reports.text: Fishing is good, with catfish biting well on trotlines and both crappie and bass producing good action north of Highway 59.
reports.by: Chad Kinsfather, Lavaca Navidad River Authority

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Fishing with topwaters for the first hour of the day and getting some fish that way, then quickly switch over to slabs to finish filling the cooler. Topwaters, swimbaits and slabs have been working on active schools near the islands and on bluff walls. Crappie can be found on brush and structure in 15-25 feet of water.
reports.by: John Blasingame, Adventure Texoma Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing remains very slow, with no solid reports this week.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good and can be caught in grass 8-12 feet with Texas rigged worms, wacky rig senko and crankbaits. Bass are also good on brush in 15-18 feet with spoons and Texas rig worms. Crappie are slow on small jigs over brush.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are in the grass during the early hours of the morning.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake B.A. Steinhagen fishing report
reports.text: Target bass in shaded areas or submerged vegetation with a slow approach.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Look for bass shallow near reeds early and throw frogs, wake baits and other small topwaters to get bit. Later, move to deeper water and look for any schooling bass and throw clear topwaters or small swimbaits and let it sink down to the school to get a bite.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on live minnows and small jigs. Largemouth bass are good on ledges and close to structure.
reports.by: Hundley's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been better this week, catching them in 15-20 feet of water roaming and chasing shad. Largemouth are slow during the day and only a little more active at night. Crappie have been hit or miss. Crappie are numerous on timber and brush piles between 15-25 feet deep and have been best on minnows. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide. Crappie fishing is excellent anywhere from 8-30 feet of water on timber.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie bite is fair on dock poles and brush piles on minnows. Largemouth bite is decent using jigs, deep crankbaits and wacky rigged baits, near deep rock and points; white bass bite is good and hybrids are fair on main lake humps with slabs or live shad. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair to 3.65 pounds in 4-25 feet of water on trick worms and square bill cranks and topwater around the grass. Crappie are good to 13 inches on minnows and jigs in 12-25 feet on deeper large docks with brush on the main lake and on scattered brush piles. White bass are slow to 1.25 pounds on crappie jigs and minnows out of the lights at night. Catfish are good to 15 pounds on jug lines with cut shad on the main lake flats and minnows around the docks mixed in with the crappie.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: Bass continue to be good on brush piles and the dam.
reports.by: Landon Hernandez, Aggie Anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Striper and black bass action has been slow.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is showing signs of improvement with some good catches being reported.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Good go-to setups include a variety of slabs, spinners and the always-reliable yellow bladed Bo Blade spinner using the proven saw tooth retrieve technique.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck's Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Bank fishing has been good, with catfish, crappie, white bass, and a variety of bait options producing solid action.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have been biting well on minnow in about 30 feet of water. Bass are hitting topwater lures, especially during early morning hours.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has been slow overall, but soft plastics are producing the best results in 7-10 feet of water.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are biting consistently around offshore structure and deeper docks on crankbaits, jigs, and soft plastics. Crappie are fair to poor, holding tight to brush piles, standing timber, and submerged structure in 15-25 feet using slower presentations with minnows or jigs. Being productive using slabs, spoons, or live shad on flats and drop-offs in 14-30 feet.
reports.by: Bradley Doyle, Bradley's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Corpus Christi Lake fishing report
reports.text: Water temperature is excellent for bass fishing, but no bass reports likely due to limited lake access.
reports.by: Glenwood Weber, Weber's Landing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been better this week, catching them in 15-20 feet of water roaming and chasing shad. Crappie have been hit or miss. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are fair on slabs. Crappie are fair on deep water brush piles. Black bass are fair early and late evening on topwater baits.
reports.by: Captain Bobby Mann, Catch a Dream Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Grass is looking good, so cast a frog to see if you can get a bass to bite. Bass are good in 20 feet of water biting deep diving crankbaits, shaky heads and Carolina rigs.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Georgetown fishing report
reports.text: Bass are deeper and a shaky head works wonders on this lake around offshore humps and ledges.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is slow but okay in shallow brush using minnows and jigs. Sand bass and hybrids are schooling around the hot water outlet and are good on slabs and shad. Bass fishing is slow but okay in shallow water vegetation.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Slabs work good on the sand bass and small striped bass when on humps and ridges in 12-20 feet of water. Largemouth bass are schooling early with the sand bass near feeding flats and are good on topwater baits and lipless crankbaits. Bigger largemouth to 7 pounds are possible on crankbaits and soft plastics fished near creek entrances and near main lake points. Some great largemouth action mid-lake is reported near Water Edge and Ports O Call. Crappie action is good to excellent on small jigs and minnows fished near underwater structures such as bridge pilings and submerged trees in the 10-20 foot depth range.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are doing well in shallow cover around points and boat ramps. Crappie are good on jigs and minnows fished over brush piles. White bass are good on slab spoons fished over humps and ridges out from the dam.Blue catfish are fair on jug lines baited with shad.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell's Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are hitting hard in the East Fork and Luces Bayou, stacked in the thermocline and feeding on minnows and hand-tied jigs. Largemouth bass in a true summer pattern, holding to deeper drop-offs and boat docks.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Inks fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in shallow water with moving baits like weedless swimbaits or spinnerbaits near shallow vegetation and docks before 9 a.m. Target bass in 10-20 feet of water submerged vegetations or rock piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are being caught on brush and underwater structure with big worms on Texas rigs, shaky heads, and dropshots.
reports.by: Greg Lotun

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have slowed down and changed their eating habits– some days they're munching, some days they don't move, and some days "where are they?" Black bass are good with white and chartreuse spinnerbaits in the mornings along with jerkbaits and soft plastics like the original Slugo worked Texas rigged without weight. White slabs 1 ounce with treble hooks cut off except one work best at Little Ridge Point, Hybrid Point, and the island tip. Tying a jig 12 inches above your slab on a loop knot catches two fish at a time.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Slabs, spoons, spinners and live bait are working. Crappie are slow to fair in 15-28 feet of water.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: Ducktracker slabs have been the ticket. Largemouth have been good on swim jigs and hitting rocks on wind blown points with square bill crankbaits.
reports.by: Michael Richardson, Lake Livingston Adventures

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Marble Falls fishing report
reports.text: Target bass in the shade of docks on the deeper side of the lake by skipping baits and jigs beneath to target bass in the shade.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair along the hydrilla with Texas and wacky rigged worms. Crappie are good on minnows in 20-30 feet suspended in brush and standing timber.
reports.by: Hambone Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is good, with sand bass being caught all over the lake - gray or pink jig-heads with red eyes paired with pearl blue or pearl white grubs are producing well. White jerkbaits, rattling shad, and minnows have also been effective for both largemouth and smallmouth. Crappie fishing is fair, with catches coming from Sanford Yake area, Blue West, and the shallows around Fritch Fortress.
reports.by: Dave Wright, Wright-On Bait, Tackle and Watercraft Rental

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on Carolina rigs and dropshots around 15-20 feet of water in the deep water. Crappie are excellent on standing timber for the big ones. Crappie fishing has been really good.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass fishing is good on Carolina rigs and medium diving crankbaits in 15-20 feet of water around deep drop-offs off of points. Crappie fishing has been excellent on white and chartreuse jigs in the standing timber.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: The largemouth bass bite has been good flipping soft plastics around reed bases in 1-3 feet of water. The bass are staying in the shallows but seeking the shadiest places possible around reeds. The key is to cover water until you find a good stretch that holds multiple bass. Crappie are fair around main lake boat docks on chartreuse jigs and catfish were fair on cut bait and stink bait around river channel bends.
reports.by: Riley Hindes, Angelo State Fishing Team

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on brush in 12-18 feet of water on minnows. Bass are slow but a few are being caught around docks in the shade.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are biting in deep water on the bottom with minnows and doing real good. Sand bass and bass are not too great this time of year due to warm water temps.
reports.by: David Holt, Lake Palo Pinto RV Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Bass are excellent now on topwater baits and Carolina rigs around grass lines. Crappie are fair on white and chartreuse jigs in timber.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow and relating to brush piles in 12-15 feet of water. Crappie are at bridge columns.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are starting to move out deep to deep brush in 35-40 feet and in trees in 25-40 feet of water. Largemouth bass are roughly the same as they've been on offshore rocks or shallow brush. Dan's Crappie Co.
reports.by: Daniel Koberna, Lt. Dan's Crappie Co

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair with fish being caught on slabs on points, humps and roadbeds on both the Richland and Chambers Creek arms of the lake. Black bass can be caught early on topwater on wind blown points. Bait are always gathering around bridges which attract the bass.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At the Marina crappie bite is fair, bluegill are fair on crickets and worms, and catfish are fair on minnows and punch bait. On the lake crappie are good on jigs and minnows over brush in 8-15 feet of water with late afternoon bite good. Black bass are slow on crankbaits and soft plastic baits in 6-14 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Slab spoons, downriggers and swimbaits are working equally good. The crappie bite has picked up. The largemouth bite is good on frogs at daylight and working over to shallow cranks around dock legs and submerged irrigation intakes.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: After they go down, start looking for fish on the grass using slabs to catch big groups of stripers surfacing in deep water anywhere from 30-60 feet deep. Topwaters, swimbaits and slabs are working. Crappie fishing look at docks and brush in 15-20 feet of water using jigs, minnows or small shad. Largemouth and smallmouth bass fishing throw topwaters early along the rock banks and off main lake points.
reports.by: John Blasingame, Adventure Texoma Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Target bass on submerged brush and mesquite in 10-25 feet of water looking for holes in the brush with soft plastic light weighted Texas rig senkos, or creature baits in watermelon or green pumpkin.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are being caught on minnows in 16-20 feet of water. Bass are being caught in 10-12 feet of water on crankbaits and topwater. Crappie and catfish are pretty good.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good with an aggressive bite on brush in 15-20 feet of water on brush with live bait or purple and chartreuse jigs. Black bass are tough. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.
reports.by: Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow around docks with crankbaits and jigs. Crappie are fair in deeper water with minnows and shad.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: White River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on jigs and minnows in 18 feet.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are up in the main lake in brush in 15-20 feet of water. White bass fishing is fair on slabs on main lake humps in 12-15 feet of water. Largemouth bass fishing is good using soft plastics on deep structure.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie continue to be good in 15-25 feet on minnows and jigs.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on main lake points, sheer bluffs, chunk rock ledges in 15-25 feet are holding better fish.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair on jigs and artificial worms. Schooling bass are active but scattered as well. Crappie are slow over brush out to 25 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Schooling bass are good early in the discharge and several places throughout the lake later on using small swimbaits with belly weighted hooks and tiny straight tail swimbaits on round head jig heads There are some good ones deep as well.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 18-20 feet of water using live minnows. Largemouth bass and smallmouth bass are good using Texas rigged worms in the stumps.
reports.by: Benbrook Marina

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass are very slow early morning.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Channel catfish are fair around rock lines on cheese bait bass are slow.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass catches up to 6.74 pounds are fair on Hag’s F8 tornados in watermelon/red flake on the ledges and brush piles in 12-18 feet with shaky heads and on crankbaits off the rocks in 6-12 feet around the mid lake to upper end early and late. Crappie are slow around docks with brush on minnows in 15-18 feet. White bass are slow on crappie jigs, or trolling crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting good midday, also right before dark while the sun is going down.
reports.by: the Aggie Anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are slow to fair, but can be caught off main lake points or ledges, and shallow rock piles in 8-12 feet of water. Crappie are good on timber 20 feet of water. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Blue catfish are being caught out in the mouth of 181 cove on cut bait channel cats are being caught around weed lines on cheese bait bass are slow Report by Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Hybrids and white bass are good early in the morning at daylight on midlake points and drop-offs along sandy flats throughout the dam area, Crappie Island, Key Ranch and the spillway humps in 13-19 feet. Cast spinners and slabs and look for schooling fish on these flats as well as deeper seawalls and shorelines. Use spinnerbaits or drop a slab down to the bottom and work it fast up and down and the fish will hit it immediately. Also throwing out a slab and reeling it back with a slow retrieve is also working well. Hit up seawalls close to points in depths of 5-18 feet and cast rattle traps, spoons, slabs or sassy shads to get the hybrids to bite. The crappie bite has been getting better…
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair early in the morning or late in the afternoon on long extended points with watermelon colored soft plastic worms and flukes. Bass are chasing shad. Crappie are biting in brush piles in 20-30 feet of water on minnows or chartreuse and black grub.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Bass up to 5 pounds have been caught. Crappie are slow.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass shallow early and chasing schools of bait after sun rises. Crappie are hit-or-miss in 13-21 feet. Hybrids and white bass are schooling in 14-23 feet, using live shad and large minnows, or trolling with a deep diver with a pet spoon as a trailer, or vertically jigging white or chartreuse slabs.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent in 20-25 feet of water on brush piles with minnows. Bass are good on deep water points and boat docks with deep jigs, diving crankbaits, dropshots and Texas rigs.
reports.by: Joey Crews, Lake Bob Sandlin Chubby Chaser Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: The early morning bass bite has been slow, but a few can be caught on windy points with spook type baits and chatterbaits in 2-5 feet. Bass are feeding in 10-12 feet where the thermocline is not present. Look for schooling bass in the open water and creeks as shad hatch is in full swing. Also, check out the brush piles as big bass are using them to feed on crappie. Crappie fishing on Lake Fork has continued to be excellent. We are seeing some big white crappie on timber in 18-28 feet along creek channels.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is tough. Bass are out on deep brush. Crappie fishing is good out in 15 feet deep brush.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair to good on trolled baits and slabs from in town by the Shores to Indian Harbor in 10-15 feet of water. Largemouth bass are fair to good on deep diving crankbaits and soft plastics worked near humps and ridges off of creek channels. Crappie fishing is good on small minnows and jigs fished off of standing timber from near Waters Edge to Decordova Bend Subdivision.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good to 5 pounds on worms and crankbaits fished up river and around main lake cover. Crappie are good on jigs and minnows fished over cover in 6-12 feet of water.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are in the shallows early around structure roaming off to submerged points and docks when the water heats up being caught on swim baits, worms and grubs. Crappie are good in Luce Bayou fishing structure in 8-14 feet of water.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass bite continues to be tough, some schoolers caught on topwater and swimbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 20 feet of water over brush piles with jigs or minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Slabs, jigs, and live bait are working. Crappie are fair in 6 to 26 foot of water. Largemouth bass and spotted bass are grouping up in 3-6 fish schools chasing bait fish in open water, or sitting around brush piles and natural structure.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Fresh willow tree piles continue to be the best cover for largemouth and crappie. Largemouth bass are good in 3-11 feet of water on Texas rig, Carolina rig, finesse jig, swim jig and at topwater frog if you can find the grass. Crappie are suspended in 8-14 feet of water on brush piles, standing timber and power line pylons on minnows. If you want to attract crappie, fresh willow trees are the best for making brush piles.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair to good on deep brush piles using redbug worms and 6XD crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on standing timber and hard spots with a Carolina rig or deep crankbait in 15-20 feet of water. The size of bass are 2-4 pounds on average. Crappie are fair in brush with ⅛ ounce white or chartreuse crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent on Carolina rigs and small paddle tail swimbaits in 8-12 feet of water. Crappie are excellent with numbers around standing timber.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair with catches up to 9 pounds on creature baits such as a rage tail Space Monkey or rage bug in Okeechobee Craw colors flipped and thick cover 4-8 feet. Crappie really good on minnows suspended 6-18 feet in trees 20-25 feet.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are biting about 3 feet off the bottom and brush piles and tree stumps own live minnows.
reports.by: David Holt, Lake Palo Pinto RV Park and Resort

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent with fish varying from2-5 pounds. Bass are in timber suspended over 20 feet about 8 feet below the surface using big swimbaits, small 5 inch white swimbaits, and dropshots. Crappie are fair with fish scattered and very few on brush piles with crappie jigs or live minnows.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Use live shad or small slabs and jigs or rattle traps. Bass are scattered on ledges, points, and deep timber hitting crankbaits, Carolina rigs, dropshots. Report by JK Outdoors Bass Fishing Guide.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Fish and a horizontal presentation throwing Bo-Blade slabs and slow rolling. Crappie are fair and relating to brush 24-35 feet deep suspended around 16-20 feet with minnows working best. Crappie are showing up suspended on bridge piles.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Hydrilla is surfacing and could be a good place to cast for bass. Bass are slow in shallow water in brush with many smaller fish being caught on frogs, and spinnerbaits. Deeper bass bite is fair with Carolina rigs. Crappie are slow moving to and from the brush to timber. Bass are feeling the heat as well. Bass are biting on finesse baits, dropshot or jig head minnow or Carolina rig.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At the Somerville Marina crappie bite is slow, bluegill and catfish are fair. Crappie are fair on jigs and minnow on main lake brush in 8-16 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair with increased angler traffic targeting the species. Bass are fair but should improve with the promise of cooler weather.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass fishing has had to transition away from reliance on hydrilla-related patterns due to the total loss of this reservoir's hydrilla due to extended flooding in May and June.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texana fishing report
reports.text: Crappie and bass are fair on the north end.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Small top waters, slabs and live bait are working depending on the school and depth. Crappie fishing is slow on hair jigs and paddle tail jigs swam slowly above brush and on structure. Bass fishing is okay throwing top waters early on main lake points and sand flats. Striped bass are good with a slab bite one day and the next on topwaters.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Guaranteed Guide Service Lake Texoma

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow too, but the few that are being caught are good size, these coming on minnows on standing trees and brush piles.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is tough and a pattern has not emerged.
reports.by: Randal Frisbie, Central Texas Fishing Guide, LLC

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow in cover in 7-10 feet of water in brush with live bait or jigs.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Night fishing is good for catfish and crappie in the lights. Crappie are slow using minnows on brush in 16-25 feet of water. Bass are slow in 10-12 feet of water with topwaters, spinnerbaits and crankbaits.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with schooling action on sunny days. Catching lots of bass throwing worms mostly with some still on frogs and flukes and on swimbaits when they are schooling. There is a good bass bite early in shallow water.
reports.by: David Townsend, Austin Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair with the best bite in the crappie house and deep brush piles with minnows. Bass are slow on deeper water ledges with crankbaits and soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie continue to be good in 15-30 feet on minnows.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on chunk rock points, ledges, and steep bluffs topwaters, weightless senkos, wacky rigs, Ned rigs, and weight less flukes.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: The shallow bass bite has been a little slow lately because a lot of fish have pulled out deep to suspend around bait.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on windy points early in the morning with shaky heads and chatterbaits in 3-7 feet.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Bass are very slow.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie continue to be good on minnows and jigs. Largemouth bass have been tough though occasional big fish are being caught. Chartreuse slabs will put them in the boat.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair with catches up to 5.68 pounds on Hag’s F5 tornados in Blue flake on the ledges with shaky heads and on cranks off the rocks and brush piles in 12-20 feet around the mid lake to upper end early and late. Crappie are slow around docks with brush on minnows in 15-18 feet. White bass are fair on crappie jigs, trolling crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Schooling bass are surfacing for some good topwater action with topwater lures or flukes.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Blue catfish are good in front of the crappie wall on cut bait. Largemouth bass are slow.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass fishing is good fishing offshore structure with brush nearby using crankbaits, football jigs, and worms. Some bass are also starting to suspend chasing balls of bait in creek channels. Crappie fishing has been hit-or-miss in 13-21 feet of water. Hair jigs from Lone Star Crappie Jigs have been producing better than plastics. White or chartreuse slabs from MT Pockets have been working well, vertical jigging.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow suspended in deep water.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good early morning around bream beds in 3-6 feet with chatterbaits and square bills crankbaits. Deep crankbaits are still good around roadbeds and humps and over deep crappie brush puked. Bass are feeding in 10-12 feet where the thermocline is not present. Look for schooling bass in the open water and creeks as shad hatch is in full swing. Also, check out the brush piles as big bass are using them to feed on crappie. The crappie fishing on Lake Fork has been improving as we approach the later part of summer. We still are seeing tons of crappie on brush piles and lay downs. They are mostly black crappie as well. We are also seeing white crappie on timber in 18-32 feet.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is fair on deeper brush. Bass are feeding early and late. Some bass are out in deeper water in brush and some are under and around docks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good early and late near creek entrances and near deeper docks. Best baits for largemouth include crankbaits and soft plastics. Crappie continue to be suspended near the thermocline on timber and bridge pilings. Small jigs and minnows are putting crappie in the boat.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair on humps in 24 feet of water with slabs and jigs or trolling with pet spoons.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth are great in the rivers early in the morning on worms and grubs. Crappie are abundant in the East fork and Luces Bayou on structure in 8-14 feet of water with small hands tied jigs.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught at night dragging a big 10 inch worm. Crappie can be caught on deep brush with minnows.
reports.by: Gilbert Miller, GTB Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are great with 1/32-1/8 ounce jigs or minnows on laydowns in 9-18 feet of water and any kind of hard structure, and brush piles in 15 feet of water. Black bass are in 3-20 feet of water biting white and chartreuse spinnerbaits early in the morning. On days bass do not react to a reaction bait, such as a crankbait, slow down your approach with a Carolina rig or Texas rig to entice a bite. If they do not pop up by 7:30 a.m., hit the main lake points and ledges in 15-20 feet with topwater plugs and swimbaits for surfacing fish, or a 1 ounce white slab for when fish are related to the bottom. Do not be surprised if you catch crappies while targeting bluegills.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good in 3-11 feet of water on Texas rig, Carolina rig, finesse jig, swim jig and at topwater frog if you can find the grass. Crappie are suspended in 8-14 feet of water on brush piles, standing timber and power line pylons on minnows. If you want to attract crappie, fresh willow trees are the best for making brush piles.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair with the early bite the best. Crappie are excellent on brush piles in 25-30 feet using Bobby Garland jigs in screamer color and minnows.
reports.by: Hambone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent on deep diving crankbaits and Carolina rigs in 18-22 feet of water. Crappie are fair in brush with live minnows, and a 1/16 or ⅛ ounce white crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Plus-1 got the most bites over the weekend for bass. If you find bass hugging the bottom in 8-10 feet dragging a Texas rig or Swing-head can be effective. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent in the timber on Carolina rigs and large swimbaits in 8-10 feet of water. Crappie are excellent on light weighted crappie jigs or live minnows.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are slow with catches up to 7 pounds and one 12 pounder caught last week. Black bass being caught on 10 inch worms in red bug and plum suspended around trees. Crappie still good suspended in trees minnows have been working best. Trees 15-20 feet but most crappie are suspended about 6-8 feet.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are great in 8-10 feet of water around boat docks and brush piles.
reports.by: David Holt, Lake Palo Pinto RV Park and Resort
