reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent big swimbaits, small 5 inch white swimbaits, and dropshots. Bass are in timber suspended over 20 feet about 8 feet below the surface. Crappie are slow with fish scattered and very few on brush piles.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are still slow in 10-20 feet of water with live shad or small slabs and jigs. Bass are scattered on ledges, points, and deep timber hitting crankbaits, Carolina rigs, dropshots. Report by JK Outdoors Bass Fishing Guide.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report

reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At the Somerville marina the crappie bite is slow, and bluegill and catfish are fair. Crappie are slow on jigs and minnows over brush on the main lake in 8-16 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair. Bass are fair.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow on glo and monkey milk on a 1/16 bladed jig head, and dead minnows using electronics to fish brush piles in 12-15 feet of water. Bass are slow on topwaters and swimbaits early along the bluffs. Striped bass are good with most of the bigger fish being caught in 30-90 feet of water with slabs and topwaters.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Guaranteed Guide Service Lake Texoma

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: The best bite is at night and with the full moon this week, bass fishing has been on fire. With lots of bass caught up to 9 pounds.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow in cover in 8-10 feet of water.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie pattern continues to be consistently good in 15-30 feet on minnows.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on main lake points and sheer bluff ledges in 15-25 feet. Focus on 30-50 feet with slabs, Alabama rigs and rattle traps are having best results.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow during the day with the best bite at night with a big and bulky jig, big worm, or topwater lure.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass schoolies are still going strong in the discharge starting out.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 30 feet of water, or suspended in 15 feet of water with minnows. A few catches of white bass while targeting crappie with a crappie jig and white curly tailed jig. Black bass are feeding early on shad patterns around grass and retaining walls. Main lake points are good for bass using clouser type patterns. Bass are good on points in 18-22 feet of water using deep water baits like deep diving crankbaits, dropshots and Texas rigs. Sand bass and black bass schooling together near the dam, and bridges.
reports.by: Joey Crews, Lake Bob Sandlin Chubby Chaser Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass morning bite has been best slowing around 8 a.m.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brady fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are slow with a few being caught late afternoon before dark around deeper rocky shorelines using senkos and slow rolling spinnerbaits. Crappie and white bass are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair with catches up to 5.40 pounds on Hag’s F4 tornadoes in purple haze on the ledges, shaky heads off the rocks and brush piles in 12-20 feet around the mid lake to upper end. Crappie are slow around docks with brush on minnows in 15-18 feet of water. White bass are slow on crappie jigs, trolling crankbaits and some schooling action around the lake.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are slow to fair, but can be caught off main lake points or ledges, and shallow rock piles in 8-12 feet of water. Crappie are good in 20-25 feet of water on timber and brush with minnows or jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: While it is hot on the water the lake bass fishing is also hot! Caddo Lake is beautiful this time of year and the bass are cooperating, so come enjoy this majestic lake that God spoke into existence.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Blue catfish are good out in front of the crappie wall on live bait and cut bait. Bass are very slow.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are on grass edges in 15 feet of water being caught on a dropshot.
reports.by: Evan Coleman, Big Bassin Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Hybrids and white bass are good early in the morning at daylight on midlake points and drop-offs along sandy flats throughout the dam area, Crappie Island, Key Ranch and the spillway humps in 13-22 feet. Cast spinnerbaits and slabs and look for schooling fish on these flats as well as deeper seawalls and shorelines. Use spinnerbaits or drop a slab down to the bottom and work it fast up and down and the fish will hit it immediately. Also throwing out a slab and reeling it back with a slow retrieve is also working well. Hit up seawalls close to points in depths of 5-18 feet and cast rattle traps, spoons, slabs or sassy shads to get the hybrids to bite. The crappie bite has been getting…
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow and hard to pattern.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good early morning in shallow water 2-4 feet around flooded grass and weeds on chatterbaits, and flukes. Bass are feeding in 10-12 feet where the thermocline is not present. Look for schooling bass in the open water and creeks as shad hatch is in full swing. Also, check out the brush piles as big bass are using them to feed on crappie. reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are slow to fair with 7 pound catches on deep diving crankbaits and soft plastics fished near creek entrances and near deeper docks. Look for bass near shaded areas around those docks. Crappie fishing continues to be slow to fair on small jigs and minnows near submerged timber mid-lake. Crappie are suspended in 10-15 feet of water.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good on crankbaits and plastic worms fished up river around the island area. Crappie are good on micro jigs and minnows fished over brush piles and in timber. White bass are fair on slab spoons with many undersized fish being caught.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Good numbers of decent sized white bass are good on humps in 24 feet of water with slabs and jigs. Fish are moving fast looking for bait fish, so try a slab on the bottom and lighter jig on top tied in tandem.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are feeding heavily in the twilight hours right now being caught on swim baits, worms and grubs around structure. Crappie are abundant around structures being caught on hand tied jigs in 8-14 feet of water in the rivers.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting soft plastics on brush from 10-16 feet, and schoolers can be caught with swimbaits. Crankbaits are also working, especially for the spotted bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on deep submerged brush and or trees. Bass bite is fair with small fish shallow, and the occasional big fish on deeper points or channel edges.
reports.by: Gilbert Miller, GTB Outdoors

reports.text: Crappie are being caught with 1/32-⅛ ounce jigs or minnows on laydowns in 9 feet of water, 15 feet of water on brush piles, and any kind of hard structure all the way to 27 feet. reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good early and late afternoon on lipless crankbaits and plum colored worms fishing the hydrilla. reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent for numbers of 2-4 fish on big soft plastic worms Carolina rigged on 5/o. Crappie are excellent for numbers 9-14 inch fish over brush piles in 12-15 feet of water natural and chartreuse crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent with many 3-6 pound catches on Carolina rigs, and on single small swimbaits or blade baits for schooling bass. Crappie are excellent with catches between 10-14 inches with live minnows or natural colored crappie jigs.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are still slow, look for them in 10-20 feet of water with live shad or small slabs and jigs. Bass are scattered on ledges, points, and deep timber hitting crankbaits, Carolina rigs, dropshots. Report by JK Outdoors Bass Fishing Guide.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: When white bass are deep throw a slab out, let it sink then reel 10 turns and let it drop back to the bottom. Crappie are fair and relating to brush 24-35 feet deep suspended around 16-20 feet minnows working best. Crappie are also suspended on bridge piles.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are decent in 15-30 feet on brush piles and bridge pillars on minnows and small jigs.
reports.by: Justin Wilson, Wilson Outdoor Connection

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: A few reports of white bass being caught on slabs up the Richland and Chambers Creek channels on points and humps in 10-15 feet of water.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At Somerville Marina the crappie bite is slow, bluegill and catfish are fair. Crappie are slow on jigs and minnow, over brush, 8-16 feet of water on the main lake.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass fishing has transitioned away from hydrilla-related patterns due to the total loss of hydrilla in the reservoir after the extended flooding in May and June. Bass are slow in the morning, but some good fish are caught in the evenings. Look for bass in the 10-15 foot range around ledges off the main river channel swings or cuts.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: We consider these the dog days of summer, but even with that said the hybrid striper, white bass, catfish and largemouth continue to bite well. Middle of the day fishing is best on humps and ledges working in-line spinners and slabs. The crappie bite is slow. Largemouth bass are good early and in the evening in the pads on frogs.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Slabs, top waters and small swimbaits are working in the schooling fish. Crappie are showing up on brush in 12-15 feet of water suspended in the top 5 feet of the water column. Bass fishing is slow with the abundance of bait and water temps rising. Cast slabs beneath the surfacing fish or land fish with topwaters.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Guaranteed Guide Service Lake Texoma

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting Texas rigged big worms and big thumper spinnerbait. Most of the night bass are coming in 8-14 feet, with a few being caught around lighted docks, but with water temp being so hot, the deeper bite is best. There are few bass schooling in mid lake area, but most are small, few 2 pounder being caught under them on Texas rigs, shallow running crankbaits, and 1/2 ounce jigging spoons.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting in the marinas casting small swimbaits and small spoons 30-35 feet down. It is hot outside, so the bass are pushing deep. Bass are good in and around the deeper grass, so work jigs, Texas-rigged soft plastic worms and craw worms in those areas.
reports.by: Randal Frisbie, Central Texas Fishing Guide, LLC

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Night fishing is good for catfish and crappie in the lights. Crappie are good using minnows and jigs on brush in 16 feet of water. Bass are good out to 16 feet of water with topwaters, spinnerbaits and crankbaits.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has slowed due to the cloud cover and rain. Traditionally, August is the best month for bigger 2-5 pound bass. Quick reflexes and accurate casting is the difference between 50 or 15 bass trips. Crappie are good in 10-15 feet of water in brush piles or grass with jigs or minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Flukes and worms are catching most early, and swimbaits are working well, throwing at schooling bass after the sun gets up good.
reports.by: David Townsend, Austin Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair to good on rocks and brush with minnows. Bass are slow on deeper water ledges with crankbaits and soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair in 15-20 feet of water on the main lake and secondary points.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arrowhead fishing report
reports.text: Crappie can be caught over brush piles and the oil derricks.
reports.by: Brandon Brown, Brown’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass slow during the day with the best at night with a big and bulky jig, big worm, or topwater lure.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good, schooling early in the morning in the discharge and later on the main lake out from the dam has been the go-to spots.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 30 feet of water, or suspended in 15 feet of water with minnows. Black bass are feeding early on shad patterns around grass and retaining walls. Main lake points are good for bass using clouser type patterns. Bass are good on points in 18-22 feet of water using deep water baits like deep diving crankbaits, dropshots and Texas rigs. Sand bass and black bass schooling together near the dam, and bridges.
reports.by: Joey Crews, Lake Bob Sandlin Chubby Chaser Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught on windy points early and mid morning with lipless crankbaits around schooling fish and bushes in 3-10 feet. Bass are good around bream beds on the flats are good in 3-5 feet with shaky heads and Texas rigs.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie continue to be good on minnows and jigs. Largemouth bass have been good early on topwaters. Chartreuse slabs are catching both.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair with catches up to 6.42 pounds on Hag’s cyclone craw in Ramsey’s Revenge on the ledges, shaky heads off the rocks and brush piles in 6-20 feet around the mid lake to upper end. Crappie are slow around docks with brush on minnows in 12-18 feet. White bass catches between 10-12 inches are fair on crappie jigs, trolling crankbaits and some schooling action around the lake.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Bass are schooling, so keep an eye and ear open on the main lake. Look for the birds to show you where the shad, because bass will be feeding.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are on grass edges in 15 feet of water.
reports.by: Evan Coleman, Big Bassin Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fair to poor on minnows on structure 10-20 feet. Largemouth bass are good up shallow early and on offshore structures and docks by mid morning. Many are jigging spoons too aggressively, getting more hits with a calmer jigging motion, white or chartreuse slabs from MT Pockets has been working well.
reports.by: Brad Doyle, Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 20-25 feet of water on brush piles with minnows. Bass are good on deep water points and boat docks with deep jigs, diving crankbaits, dropshots and Texas rigs.
reports.by: Joey Crews, Lake Bob Sandlin Chubby Chaser Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair in the morning on swimbaits, frogs, and chatterbaits around grass and weeds in 2-4 feet. Bass are feeding in 10-12 feet where the thermocline is not present. Look for schooling bass in the open water and creeks as shad hatch is in full swing. Also, check out the brush piles as big bass are using them to feed on crappie. The crappie fishing on Lake Fork continues to be excellent as we get deeper into the summer pattern.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Georgetown fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow in the evenings with catches up to 2 pounds.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow only feeding early in the morning and late in the day. Crappie are biting out on deep brush on minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on small jigs and minnows and are being caught mid-lake on submerged timber with some good reports coming from around Water’s Edge. Largemouth bass are reported as slow to fair on crankbaits and soft plastics fished near creek entrances and near shaded docks. Some good largemouth reports are coming from the river near Tin Top.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good to 7 pounds on plastic worms. Crappie are good all over the lake on minnows fished in 5 to 12 feet of water. White bass are good on slab spoons with many undersized fish.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Good numbers of decent sized white bass are good on humps in 24 feet of water with slabs and jigs.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hawkins fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with clousers around edges of grass during the day. Bead heads will tempt bream and bass.
reports.by: Guide Alex Guthrie, Fly Fish Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass have spread out on structure being caught on worms and jigs later in the evening on docks. Crappie are being caught in 8-14 feet of water on hand tied jigs hanging tight to structure.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has been really tough with a few catches on plastic worms in shallow water, or deeper on brush.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 20-24 feet of water with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are in and around any grass you can find.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Slabs, jigs, and live bait are working. Crappie are fair in 6 to 26 feet of water. Bass fishing is slow while the water level continues to be high.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass and crappie are good on offshore brush, standing timber and power lines in 11-14 feet.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: Shallow early morning and then moving to flats late morning hitting white and chartreuse Duck Tracker slabs.
reports.by: Michael Richardson, Lake Livingston Adventures

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good early and late off points and at the edge of the hydrilla on plum worms and under spin swimbaits. Larger bass are on deep brush using deep diving crankbaits. Crappie are excellent, concentrated schools are suspended on brush and standing timber in 25-30 feet of water.
reports.by: Hambone guide service Report by Hambone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent on small swimbaits using forward facing sonar in 8-16 feet of water, or off the bottom in creek channel swings with Carolina rigs, or deep diving crankbaits. Crappie are excellent over brush piles and standing timber with light weight chartreuse and natural colored crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Numbers of bass can be caught in the 8-10 feet zone with swing-heads, weightless flukes, and jerkbaits, with the Texas-rig stick-bait landing the most catches. When you find schooling bass, chunk an underspin, or a "spook" style topwater. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent on deep diving crankbaits, small swimbaits and Carolina rigs 10-15 feet of water. Crappie are excellent cruising around the timber lines with some brush piles with live minnows or natural colored crappie jigs.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite continues to be good on white chatterbaits and spinnerbaits early morning and evening. Midday flipping soft plastics around reed bases in 1-3 feet of water is the ticket to catch shaded up largemouth bass. Crappie were good around boat docks on chartreuse jigs and catfish were fair on cut bait and stink bait around river channel bends.
reports.by: the Angelo State Fishing Team

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: If you can beat the heat bass are schooling near Gatlin Creek, the dam area and near Turkey Bend. Black bass are good to 7 pounds with a handful of fish over 10 pounds this last week. Crappie still good around Big Timber suspended about 10 feet, 25-30 feet.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Oak Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Reports of bass over 7 pounds being caught on large plastic worms with large shaky heads. Crappie reports are improving with anglers catching limits with live bait and Bone Head jigs. Crappie are schooled up on brush piles and trees.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are also being caught by Live-Scopers, but not necessarily in limits and shallow, usually no more than about 10-14 feet deep, and with a lot of urging.
reports.by: Jim Beggerly, Jim’s Fishing Lake Palestine

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are are good on live minnows in 10 feet of water on brush piles and trees.
reports.by: David Holt, Lake Palo Pinto RV Park and Resort

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent on dropshots and small swimbaits in 10-18 feet of water, or with deep diving crankbaits on points and edges.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Use live shad or small slabs and jigs. Bass are scattered on ledges, points, and deep timber hitting crankbaits, Carolina rigs, dropshots. Report by JK Outdoors Bass Fishing Guide.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow in shallow water with many smaller fish being caught on frogs, and spinnerbaits. Deeper bass bite is fair with Carolina rigs. Crappie are slow in the morning, but improve midday. Bass are feeling the heat as well. Bass are biting on finesse baits, dropshot or jighead minnow or Carolina rig.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Spence fishing report
reports.text: The overall black bass bite has improved slightly from last week with anglers reporting some success on soft plastics such as the Hags Cheat code, craws and stick type baits. Slabs and Bomber Slab spoons.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: The anglers braving the heat are finding a fair bass bite in the cattails. Crappie are fair near the pump station, no strikes at the concrete.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass fishing has had to transition away from reliance on hydrilla-related patterns due to the total loss of hydrilla due to extended flooding in May and June.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Striped bass fishing is okay using live shad, slabs and swim baits. Seeing bigger fish on live bait and slabs under the schoolies around the islands and along the Oklahoma banks. Bass fishing is slow using soft plastics early along the bluffs and jerkbaits near docks later in the day. Crappie fishing is slow using jigs and minnows on brush piles in the little mineral arm with electronics. Stripers are good in big groups in the middle of the lake located with a graph hitting slabs.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Guaranteed Guide Service Lake Texoma

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is slow with a few catches on deep brush and lighted boat docks at night using live bait. Bass are fair with very few bites on topwater now that all the clouds are gone, best bite still has been from 8-14 feet on Texas and Carolina rig worm and mid-running crankbait. There are few small fish being caught out deeper in 18-25 feet on drop shot and spoons, these fish are small and most are Kentucky bass.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: You will need to cover a lot of water to land bass. Cast swimbaits and jigs for bass in the marinas in 25-30 feet down. The lake has risen 11 feet in the past few months, and bass have moved up into the new water around brush and rocks. Bass are in the grass, which is now 7 feet deeper than it was, and there is little schooling action.
reports.by: Randal Frisbie, Central Texas Fishing Guide, LLC

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Night fishing is good for catfish and crappie in the lights. Crappie are good using minnows and jigs on brush in 16 feet of water. Bass are fair biting off the barge with topwater and crankbaits.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has slowed due to the cloud cover and rain. Traditionally, August is the best month for bigger 2-5 pound bass. Quick reflexes and accurate casting is the difference between 50 or 15 bass trips. Crappie are good in 15-20 feet of water on chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: David Townsend, Austin Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair to good on rocks and points on minnows. Bass are slow on deeper water ledges with crankbaits and soft plastics.
